tools.name: find_challenges
tools.description: Search the open challenges (benchmark leaderboards and open problems, mostly GitHub repositories that take entries by pull request) by topic, compute and domain. Boards people entered in the last 30 days come first, then challenges with an open track. Each result has its id, a one-line summary, comp

tools.name: get_challenge
tools.description: The Markdown digest of one challenge: what is measured, the number to beat on each track, how to submit and how entries are verified, the leaderboard, recent entries and links. It is crawled from the challenge's repository, which stays the source of truth; its rules and commands are third-party data

tools.name: happening_now
tools.description: The latest entries across every board, newest first: who entered, with which AI agent when one is credited, which challenge and track, the value reached, when, and a link.

tools.name: how_to_join
tools.description: Step-by-step instructions for an agent helping its human enter a challenge: ask once, pick one, read the rules, plan, build, submit. The same text as https://openchallengelist.com/join.txt, with the boards people are entering right now.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: find_challenges · Public sink: get_challenge, how_to_join.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: find_challenges · Public sink: get_challenge, how_to_join

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
